name: Arthur Online
tagline: Cloud property management for landlords, letting agents and block managers: tenancies, rent ledgers, maintenance jobs and documents in one system.

pricing.basis: monthly, tiered by number of units under management
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: If you are one person with a handful of rentals, the useful 20 percent of this is a CRUD app: properties, units, tenancies, a rent schedule, payments against that schedule, an arrears view, a maintenance log and expiring compliance certificates. An agent replaces that with a weekend of Prisma models and a few tables, and it will genuinely work. What does not survive the one-shot is everything that touches other people: tenant and contractor portals, mobile apps, open banking feeds that reconcile rent automatically, Xero sync and portal listing feeds. If you handle other people's money as an agent, the client money accounting and audit trail is the product, and a homemade ledger is a bad place to find that out.
coreLoopDIY: A local single-user app that tracks properties, tenancies and rent schedules, records payments against them, flags arrears and expiring certificates, and logs maintenance jobs with document uploads.
requirements: Node 20+ and local disk for the SQLite file and uploads
Manual CSV export from your bank if you want payment matching
Your own discipline about entering payments, since nothing syncs itself
whatYouLose: Open banking bank feeds and automatic rent reconciliation, so every payment is hand-entered or CSV-imported
Tenant and contractor portals plus mobile apps, so maintenance requests arrive by text and WhatsApp again
Accounting integrations (Xero and friends) and portal listing feeds
Client money accounting with a defensible audit trail, which matters the moment you manage for someone else
Multi-user roles, so no bookkeeper or property manager logging in alongside you
moatNotes: The regulated bit is agency client money handling and reporting, not the tenancy table. Also, once five years of ledgers live in it, nobody migrates for fun.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the software is the smallest part of the job. Agents pay for a system their accountant, auditor and clients will accept, for feeds that reconcile rent without a human squinting at a bank statement, and for portals so tenants and contractors have somewhere to go that is not a personal phone. A landlord with four units genuinely can self-host a replacement and be happier for it. A landlord with forty, or anyone holding other people's rent, is buying process and liability cover as much as features.
notes: Small self-managing landlords are the clean win here; agencies are not.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user property management app for a small private landlord. No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind, SQLite via Prisma, server actions for mutations, Zod for validation. Everything runs with `npm run dev` on localhost. File uploads go to ./uploads on local disk, not to any bucket.

Data model:
- Property: address, purchase date, notes.
- Unit: belongs to Property, label, bedrooms, current market rent.
- Tenant: name, email, phone, notes.
- Tenancy: unit, one or more tenants, start date, end date, rent amount, frequency (monthly or weekly), deposit amount, deposit scheme reference.
- RentCharge: generated rows per tenancy per period with due date and amount.
- Payment: date, amount, method, optional link to a RentCharge.
- MaintenanceJob: unit, title, description, status (open, in progress, done), contractor name, cost, dates.
- Certificate: unit, type (gas safety, EICR, EPC, other), issue date, expiry date, uploaded file.
- Document: attaches a file to any property, unit, tenancy or job.

Features in scope:
- Generate RentCharge rows for a tenancy from start date to end date or 12 months ahead.
- Record payments and allocate them to charges, allowing partial and over payments.
- Arrears screen: every tenancy with balance owed, sorted worst first.
- Dashboard: total monthly rent roll, arrears total, open jobs, certificates expiring in the next 60 days.
- CSV bank statement import: map date, description, amount columns, then suggest matches to unpaid charges by amount and rough date, with a one-click confirm. Never auto-allocate.
- Per property and per year income and expense summary, exportable as CSV.
- Full text search across tenants, properties and jobs.

Explicitly out of scope: tenant or contractor logins, email or SMS sending, open banking, accounting software sync, portal listing feeds, multi-user roles, double entry client money accounting.

Seed the database with two properties, three tenancies and some deliberately messy payments so the arrears and matching screens have something to chew on. Put the database path and upload directory in .env with a committed .env.example. Include a README covering setup, a backup command that copies the SQLite file, and a blunt note that this is not suitable for handling other people's client money.
